title: Feminist groups call for marches against gender-based violence in Paris

tea.why: Protesters are demonstrating against gender-based and sexual violence, citing systemic impunity and a lack of support for victims.
tea.want: They demand a comprehensive law against violence toward women and children, along with full budgetary funding for its implementation.
tea.changed: Nov 24: Organizers confirmed two separate routes through Paris for the November 28 demonstrations.

summary: Feminist collectives in Paris have scheduled two separate marches for November 28, 2026, to protest gender-based and sexual violence. One march, organized by the Grève féministe collective, is set to depart from the Panthéon and proceed to Place d’Italie. A second march, organized by the Nous Toutes collective, is scheduled to depart from Place de la République toward Place de la Nation. These events follow the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women. Organizers, including various unions and associations, are calling for a comprehensive law to address violence against women and children. The demonstrations are part of a broader week of mobilization across France. Authorities have not yet finalized the specific routes or potential station closures, though organizers have publicized their planned paths.
demands: Comprehensive law against violence toward women and children
Full budgetary funding for victim support
response: No official response reported in the sources.

updates.text: Feminist groups announced plans for marches in Paris on November 28.
Collectives confirmed two distinct routes for the upcoming demonstrations in the capital.
The Fondation des Femmes announced it will join the march from the Panthéon to Place d’Italie.
